newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock issue quota aims to cool down markets.
newsitem.headline: China stock issue quota aims to cool down markets.

text.p: China's decision to double the quota for new stock issues in 1997 from 1996 aims to increase the supply of stocks and curb overheating on the stock markets, the China Securities News said on Friday.
The move is also aimed at supporting major state-run firms, which will be given priority for share listings, the newspaper said in a commentary.

The Securities Commission under the State Council (cabinet) and the State Planning Commission on Thursday announced a quota for new stock issues in 1997 of 30 billion yuan, compared with the 1996 quota of 15 billion.
"The unprecedented large-scale quota indicates the authorities intend to curb the over-heated stock markets by effectively increasing stock supply," the commentary said.

The newspaper said there had been an acute shortage of shares on China's stock markets in the past year with more and more investors wanting to invest due to the healthy development of the nation's economy.
This had resulted in sharp rises in stock prices and some excessive speculation, the newspaper said.
"The new quota will be distributed with priority being given to major state enterprises and will help to curb malicious speculation in shares in small companies," the newspaper said.
"A large number of major companies coming into the markets will help stabilise them," it said.
The newspaper also said that using the quota system to adjust trading indicated the authorities wanted to use market means to control the markets.
